title: introduce-response-output-strictness-toggle-with-stream-fallback-and-openai-compat-mapping
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers using structured response_format wanted a way to gradually opt into strict JSON Schema validation without disrupting streaming-first workloads or tool-invoking flows. This PR adds a runtime-controlled strictness toggle, a prioritized stream-fallback mapping, and OpenAI-compat error-code translation so that callers receive consistent signals across compatibility layers. Design summary: 1) response_format.strictness boolean (runtime-config + per-request header override) toggles between permissive and strict validation modes. 2) When strict mode is enabled, final-block validation enforces the configured JSON Schema. If stream chunks are malformed, the runtime will attempt two recovery strategies in order: prefix-coercion attempts minimal corrective edits to reconstitute a well-formed JSON object; checkpoint-rewind falls back to the last validated checkpoint and continues generation with a softer schema profile. 3) A new stream_fallback_map lets operators prefer "coerce-first" or "rewind-first" and set maximum recovery attempts. 4) Tool/function-calling paths are fenced: when a tool call is emitted the output is validated against the declared tool-schema; if strictness rejects a tool payload it converts the rejection into a structured tool-error event instead of dropping the invocation. 5) OpenAI compatibility adapter maps internal validation error classes into stable OpenAI-style error codes and includes an error_hint payload for developer tooling. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains permissive (strictness off) unless opt-in via config or request flag. Streaming semantics: added lightweight checkpoints every N tokens (configurable) to bound rewind cost. The implementation touches the response_format negotiation layer, the runtime validator, stream checkpointing, and the openai compatibility shim. Tests and rollout: added unit and integration tests that exercise coerce-first and rewind-first strategies, toolcall fencing, and compatibility mapping. Feature toggles and telemetry allow a staged rollout starting with canary accounts. Related work: references ENG-2148 for schema negotiation design, SUP-4132 incident notes motivating clearer error codes. Checklist: - implementation and tests added - docs updated with config and semantics - SDK surface updated (python/ts) - canary rollout plan attached. See release_notes for operational guidance.

release_notes: Added a per-request and runtime toggle for structured-output strictness, stream recovery strategies (coerce-first and rewind-first), tool-call fencing behavior under strict validation, and OpenAI compatibility error mapping. Default remains permissive; operators can opt into strict mode for higher schema guarantees. See docs/operational/stream_recovery.md for rollout guidance and telemetry to monitor recovery events.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout steps included in examples/strictness_toggle/canary_playbook.md. Watch metrics 'stream.recovery.attempts' and 'stream.recovery.success_rate'. Set stream_fallback_map.max_attempts to 3 for initial rollout.
